propositions: The MCP server's sign and verify operations resolve the op-cert key from different resolution chains: signing uses the context-local startup binding (via REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY) but verification reads only from tracker-local .opcert-key.pub, causing every attestation to be uncertifiable on the same box.

On the deployed server, sign_manifest succeeds but verify_signature immediately returns verdict=foreign_key with reason 'this environment has no op-cert public key', blocking all plan-review claims and attestations.

The verify side (_opcert_own_public_key) never consults the startup binding or REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH that the sign side uses, creating a permanent key mismatch even when the tracker holds a genesis keypair.

The fix unifies both operations to resolve the public key from the same ordered chain (bound startup signer, then REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH, then tracker genesis) by deriving the public line in-process with ssh-keygen -y instead of requiring a cached .pub file.
